title: Fatality Management Specialist (Fatality Mgmt SPC)
raw_text:
10-92M. MOS 92M—Fatality Management Specialist (Fatality Mgmt SPC), CMF 92 (Eff 202510)
   a. Major duties. Performs duties relating to deceased personnel to include recovery, collection, evacuation of remains
and personal effects, and the establishment of tentative identification through postmortem data collection. Duties for MOS
92M at each level of skill are:
         (1) MOSC 92M1O. Assists with recovery of unburied dead, hasty or isolated graves, personal effects, and
identification media. Disinters remain, records personal effects, and evacuates remains and personal effects to
designated points. Determines and records recovery locations on maps, sketches, and overlays. Establishes and records
tentative identification. Assists in preparation, preservation, and shipment of remains. Inventory, safeguard, and evacuate
personal effects. Assists with temporary interment operations.
         (2) MOSC 92M2O. Plans and supervises incident site operations of deceased personnel, personal effects, and
identification media. Supervises personnel in special handling, marking, and shipping of contagious disease cases and
processing of contaminated remains. Supervises receipt, storage, and issue of supplies and equipment. Oversee
documentation and record-keeping throughout the recovery and disposition process. Train junior specialists in proper
procedures and techniques for dignified remains handling. Coordinates with relevant agencies to ensure smooth and
dignified transfer of remains.
         (3) MOSC 92M3O. Performs duties shown in previous skill level when required. Advises commanders and
headquarters staff on fatality management activities and coordinates activities of subordinate units. Establishes and
maintains liaison with support and combat units. Trains nonfatality management unit recovery teams (URTs) on search
procedures at the 20 level. Coordinates transportation requirements for deceased personnel, manage logistical
requirements. Develops and implements fatality management plans, preparing for potential contingencies. Oversee the
accurate documentation and reporting of all recovery and disposition activities. Instructs, trains and mentors’ personnel,
enhancing their expertise in fatality management procedures.
         (4) MOSC 92M4O. Coordinates with U.S. and international authorities on fatality management issues, ensuring
compliance and cooperation. Performs duties shown at the preceding skill level and provides technical guidance to junior
grade personnel. Advises staff on temporary interment locations, emergency burials, and security and disposition of
remains and personal effects. Coordinates with non-U.S. service authorities, other service authorities and civilian officials
on fatality management matters. Coordinates and advises on military burials and ceremonies. Assists in review of fatality
services contracts. Advises summary court authorities on evacuation of personal effects. Supervises fatality management
activities.
         (5) MOSC 92M5O. Supervises fatality management activities, provides technical and
administrative support on temporary interment matters, acquisition of land for temporary interment, equipment
requirements for mortuaries, and recovery/evacuation procedures. Advise on policy and procedures, contributing to
improvements in fatality management practices. Manage resources and personnel, optimize effectiveness and maintain
readiness. Serve as a subject matter expert, providing guidance and support to commanders and staff.
   b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. Fatality Management specialists must possess
the following qualifications:
         (1) A physical demands rating of Heavy (Black).
         (2) A physical profile of 222221.
         (3) Normal color vision. No aversion to the sight and handling of needles, human tissues, blood, skeletal and/or
decomposed human remains.
         (4) Per AR 600-8-19, promotion to MSG and SGM requires an interim secret eligibility or higher.
         (5) Qualifying scores.
             (a) A minimum score of 84 in aptitude area GM, effective 9 October 2023.
             (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0160 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0450 cm,
Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0160 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0043 shuttles in Physical Demand Category in “Heavy”
(Black).
         (6) Mandatory formal training. Completion of MOS 92M course conducted under the auspices of the U.S. Army
Quartermaster School. Waiver requests can be submitted to the Office of the Quartermaster Commandant Enlisted
Proponent Office at USARMY Ft Lee, VA, 23801. TRADOC List QM Enlisted Personnel Development
usarmy.lee.tradoc.list.qm-enlisted-personnel-development@army.mil.
   c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all enlisted MOS)).
         (1) D6--Operational Data Analyst (personnel only)
   d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill level are listed in
the following tables:
         (1) Table 10-92M-1. Physical requirements.
         (2) Table 10-92M-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (3) Table 10-92M-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
